title.rendered: Club Steward: One Platform for Multi-Club Golf and Country Club Operators

excerpt.rendered: How Ardn built Club Steward, a golf and country club platform that gives multi-club operators one member record, online join, e-signed contracts, autopay dues, a member app, the tee sheet and portfolio reporting.

content.rendered:
Introduction

Club Steward is golf and country club management software for operators that run more than one club. It gives a portfolio one platform and one member record for club websites and online join, membership sales, contracts, dues, the member app, the tee sheet, the pro shop, private events and reporting. Ardn designed and built Club Steward, and runs it as a managed service.

Challenge

Multi-club operators usually run each club on its own stack, and the gaps show up in the same places:

  • One member, many records. A member who belongs at one club and plays at another exists twice, with two balances and two histories.
  • Joining takes paper. Prospects fill in forms, wait for a contract, sign on a visit, and are billed by hand weeks later.
  • Leads sit with whoever answered. Nobody sees the whole sales pipeline, and a stalled lead has no one chasing it.
  • Reports stop at the club. Regional and corporate questions are answered by exporting from each club and pasting into a spreadsheet.
  • Access is all or nothing. Club staff either see too much or need head office for routine work.

Solution

1. One member record across every club

A member is one record in the portfolio, with their membership, benefits, dues, standing and activity at every club on one timeline. Reciprocal access and benefits follow the member, not the club.

2. A website and a six-step online join

Each club gets a website on the platform, and prospects join online in six steps: choose a plan, add the household, review the agreement, sign, pay and set up the member app. The record, contract and billing are created as they go.

3. A sales pipeline with a shared lead pool

Leads from every club land in one pipeline. A shared pool means a lead is never stuck with one person, and escalation rules move a stalled lead to a manager automatically.

4. Contracts, e-signature and dues

  • Contracts are generated from the plan and signed in the platform with built-in e-signature. Payment is blocked until the contract is signed.
  • Dues run on card or ACH autopay, with standing visible on the member record.

5. The member app, the tee sheet and the club floor

  • A member app with a digital membership card, benefits and bookings.
  • Tee sheet, cart assignments and the pro shop on the same records as membership.
  • Private events and catering, from inquiry to the day.

6. Reporting and security for a portfolio

  • Reports scoped to club, region or corporate, from the same library.
  • Per-club data isolation enforced in the database, so a query scoped to one club cannot read another.
  • More than 400 permissions, grouped into roles, so a pro shop clerk and a regional director each see exactly their job.

Results

  • One record per member, however many clubs they use.
  • Joining without paper: plan to signed contract to first payment, online, in six steps.
  • A sales pipeline the whole operator can see, with leads that escalate instead of stalling.
  • Answers at club, region and corporate level without a spreadsheet.
  • Club data kept apart in the database, with access shaped by role.
  • Accounting is in preview. Ardn runs the platform as a managed service.

title.rendered: A Membership and Fundraising Platform for Community Nonprofits

excerpt.rendered: How Ardn built a platform that puts members and donors on one record, with household billing, one-scan check-in, programs with waitlists and board-ready reporting, for a flat fee.

content.rendered:
Introduction

This is a membership and fundraising platform for community nonprofits: multi-branch organizations that run memberships, programs and a front desk, and raise money from the same community. Ardn designed and built the platform and runs it as a managed service. It is sold for a flat fee, never a percentage of the organization's revenue.

Challenge

  • Two systems for one person. Operations lived in one platform and donors in another, reconciled by hand every month.
  • Families are billed in messy ways. Split payers, alternating months and assistance rates rarely fit a standard subscription.
  • Peak hours at the front desk. Part-time staff needed to check in members, guests and walk-ins in seconds, not clicks.
  • Programs fill up. Classes and camps needed capacity, waitlists and rosters by branch.
  • The board asks by branch. Reports were assembled from exports.
  • Pricing that grows with the mission. Incumbent platforms often take a percentage of revenue, so every successful campaign raises the software bill.

Solution

1. Members and donors on one record

The parent who pays for swim lessons and gives to the annual campaign is one person in the system, with memberships, registrations, check-ins, gifts and volunteer hours on one timeline that the membership team and the development office both see.

2. Household billing with split payers

A household holds guardians and dependents with the billing arrangement that fits: one payer, a split, alternating months or a custom schedule. Every member has their own barcode.

3. One-scan front-desk check-in

One screen for barcodes, guest passes and name search, showing today's classes at the location and who has arrived.

4. Programs and classes with waitlists

Per-branch pricing, capacity, waitlists, rosters and attendance, with members booking from a branded portal.

5. Fundraising on the member record

Campaigns with goals and public giving pages, gifts recorded by branch and campaign, and donor records linked to the same people the front desk checks in.

6. Board-ready reporting by branch

A report library and dashboards scoped by branch and program, built so the person who is asked can answer.

7. Priced for a nonprofit

  • A flat fee, never a percentage of revenue.
  • Payments settle to the organization's own merchant account.
  • A free pilot in the organization's own branding before anyone signs.
  • A 60-day go-live guarantee.

Results

  • One record per person, whether they are a member, a donor, a volunteer or all three.
  • Families billed the way they actually pay, with split and alternating payers handled by the system.
  • Check-in in one scan, even at peak hours with part-time staff.
  • Board questions answered by branch from the same reports.
  • A software bill that stays flat as the mission grows, with money settling to the organization's own account.

title.rendered: Ardn CRM for Construction: Jobs, Service and Dispatch on One Record

excerpt.rendered: How Ardn built a CRM for roofing, home improvement and general contractors around jobs, work orders, service requests and dispatch, priced by modules and locations rather than per seat.

content.rendered:
Introduction

Ardn CRM for construction is a CRM built around jobs, work orders, sites, service requests and bookings for roofing, windows and home improvement, residential and commercial general contractors, and real estate. Ardn designed and built it and launched it as its own product; it is priced by modules and locations, never per seat, with a setup fee and an optional managed service.

Challenge

  • Generic CRMs stop at the sale. Contractors needed the deal to become a job, with sites, crews and work orders that follow.
  • Per-seat pricing kept the field out. Crew leads who needed to see a job were another license, so most of the team worked from texts.
  • Service fell through. Callbacks sat in an inbox until the customer called again.
  • Dispatch by phone. Who was where today was answered by calling around.
  • Switching means moving history. Nobody wants to lose years of accounts and notes to change tools.

Solution

1. A business-health dashboard

Pipeline value, jobs in progress, open service requests and revenue on one screen, so the owner knows how the business is doing before the Monday meeting.

2. Pipeline board and deal pages

Leads from the website, referrals and calls land in one pipeline with stages the contractor defines. Each deal page shows every call, email, visit and quote on a timeline.

3. Quotes that become jobs in one click

Quotes are built from the product and service list, so pricing is consistent across estimators. When the customer accepts, one click converts the quote into a job with its line items, site and contact already in place.

4. A service desk with SLA clocks

Every service request gets an SLA clock based on priority. Requests that are not picked up or resolved in time escalate automatically, and customers rate the visit when it closes.

5. Dispatch and work orders

A dispatch board shows crews, work orders and bookings by day and location. Assigning from the board updates the work order for the crew.

6. Accounts, reports and migration

  • Accounts hold sites, contacts, quotes, jobs and service requests for one customer, with lifetime value on the page.
  • Reports cover the conversion funnel, revenue by source and service performance.
  • Ardn migrates accounts, contacts, deals, job history and notes from the previous CRM as part of setup.

Results

  • Sales, jobs and service on one record, from the first call to the finished job.
  • The whole team in the system, because pricing follows modules and locations rather than head count.
  • No service request forgotten: SLA clocks, automatic escalation and a customer rating on every close.
  • Dispatch everyone can see, without a phone call.
  • History carried over from the previous CRM by Ardn, and an optional managed service to run it.

title.rendered: Rx-Dr: A White-Label Telehealth Platform, Built and Run by Ardn

excerpt.rendered: How Ardn built a multi-tenant telehealth platform that lets brands launch online care under their own name, with intake, clinician review, pharmacy routing, payments and HIPAA controls built in.

content.rendered:
Introduction

Rx-Dr is a white-label telehealth platform. It lets a wellness brand, medical practice or clinic group launch online care under its own name: a patient chooses a treatment, completes an online intake, a licensed clinician reviews the case, and the prescription goes electronically to a partner pharmacy that ships it. Ardn designed and built the platform, and runs it as a managed service.

Challenge

Launching a compliant telehealth brand usually means stitching together five regulated systems, each hard to build on its own:

  • Intake, clinician review, pharmacy e-prescribing, payments and patient messaging all have to work together and stay HIPAA-compliant.
  • Many brands, one platform. Brands, clinics and referral partners each need their own branded experience, with their data kept strictly apart.
  • Prescribing rules change by state and by drug, and every decision needs an audit trail.
  • Layered referral networks (agencies, sales agents, clinics and creators) need commissions, refunds and payouts that are right every time.
  • Subscriptions and refills need renewals, shipments and pharmacy resubmissions to run on their own.

Solution

1. One multi-tenant platform, many brands

Every brand gets its own domain, logo, colors and storefront, plus a separate test environment next to its live one. Tenant isolation is enforced in the data layer: a query that isn't scoped to a tenant fails instead of leaking data, and automated checks block code that would break the rule.

2. A portal for every role

Admins, operators, physicians, clinics, pharmacies, patients and referral partners each get their own portal, around 500 screens in total, all running on the same records.

3. Intake, review and prescribing compliance

  • Intake questionnaires built per treatment category, with conditional logic, clinician review flags and ID capture.
  • State-by-state and drug-by-drug prescribing rules that fail closed: if an approved rule doesn't exist for a case, the order is denied rather than allowed by default.
  • An external prescriber API so an outside clinician network can pick up cases and approve or decline them.

4. Pharmacy, payments and operations on autopilot

  • Electronic prescription transmission to partner pharmacies, with status synced back and cancellations and resubmissions handled.
  • Split payments, memberships and subscriptions, with a commission ledger that handles clawbacks and payouts across referral tiers.
  • 54 scheduled background jobs run renewals, shipments, follow-up care and data-integrity checks.
  • Patient messaging, video visits and appointment booking built in.

5. HIPAA built in, not bolted on

  • Workforce Business Associate Agreement attestations, logged access to patient records ("minimum necessary"), and break-glass access that requires a written reason.
  • Field-level AES-256 encryption for sensitive identifiers, and automated checks that keep patient data out of logs.
  • Two-person approval for sensitive admin actions, a full audit log, fraud flags and privacy tooling.
  • AI helps with document reading and clinician triage. It never approves a prescription.

Outcomes

  • A brand can launch without building a medical stack. Intake, clinicians, pharmacy routing, payments and the patient portal come ready, under the brand's name.
  • One platform, many brands. Each brand is isolated and branded, with its own test environment.
  • Compliance by design. Prescribing rules fail closed, every read of a patient record is logged, and sensitive actions need a second approver.
  • Operations that run themselves. Renewals, refills, commissions and payouts run on schedule, with integrity checks that flag anything stuck.
  • Built to scale: about 300 data models, around 500 screens and 54 automated jobs, all run by Ardn as a managed service.

Want something like this?

Rx-Dr is an example of how Ardn works: we map the business, build an AI-first platform around it, and run it for you. See our approach, or talk to us about your idea.

title.rendered: Research Only: A Compliance-First Store for a Regulated Product Category

excerpt.rendered: How Ardn built and runs a compliance-first e-commerce store for a regulated product category: eligibility confirmation and disclosures on every page, lot-level quality documents, resilient payments, a partner program and a full back office.

content.rendered:
Introduction

Research Only is a US online store in a regulated product category, where every product is sold strictly for its permitted use and every lot ships with independent quality documentation. Ardn designed and built the store and its back office, and runs it as a managed service.

Challenge

  • A regulated category. Every page has to state clearly what the products are for, who may buy them and the store's legal position.
  • Trust has to be provable. Buyers want to verify quality for the exact lot and size before they order.
  • Payments are harder than usual. The category needs resilient, multi-rail payments rather than a single provider.
  • Real operational complexity. Sizes and bundles, tiered pricing, several fulfillment partners and a partner program with commissions.
  • Organic visibility matters. With limited paid-ad options, search and AI-answer visibility carry the growth.

Solution

1. A compliance layer on every page

Visitors confirm their eligibility before entering. A permitted-use notice appears on every page and every product, and a dedicated compliance statement covers the store's regulatory position.

2. Quality documents, per lot and per size

Each product page shows verified quality data with the independent lab report available to download for every size. Documents are versioned in the database and tied to the lot they cover.

3. A storefront built to convert

  • Catalog with search, sorting and size options, plus "frequently ordered together" bundles.
  • Automatic bundle discounts with no code to remember.
  • Customer accounts with orders, addresses and notifications.
  • PCI-friendly hosted card fields, so card data never touches the store's servers, plus resilient multi-rail payments.

4. A back office that runs the business

More than 60 admin screens cover products, lots and inventory, pricing tiers and promotions, customers, the shipping queue and fulfillment routing, email templates, and a go-live checklist. Audit logging and a personal-data access log record who saw what.

5. Partner program

Partners get their own branded referral storefront links and portal, with automatic order credit and twice-monthly payout statements.

6. Search and AI-answer visibility

Every public page is pre-rendered, with structured data for products, articles and FAQs, plus a library of buyer guides. A crawler policy welcomes search and AI answer engines and blocks AI training crawlers.

Outcomes

  • Compliance built into the product: eligibility confirmation, permitted-use notices and the compliance statement ship with every page.
  • Lot-level quality documents on every product, versioned and downloadable per size.
  • 59 indexed pages, including buyer guides built for search and AI answers.
  • About 0.1-second server response on the home and product pages, served from the edge.
  • One back office for catalog, fulfillment, partners and payouts, run by Ardn as a managed service.

Want something like this?

Research Only shows how Ardn builds for regulated, complex categories: compliance, trust and operations designed in from day one. See custom e-commerce development, or talk to us about your store.

title.rendered: Revolutionizing Airline Customer Service with Salesforce Customer360 Console

content.rendered:
Introduction

A major airline recognized the need to enhance both customer and agent experiences through a centralized, efficient customer service system. To achieve this, they partnered with a leading consulting firm to implement the Salesforce Customer360 Service Console. This unified platform provided agents with seamless access to customer, loyalty, and flight data, improving service efficiency and customer satisfaction across multiple channels.

Challenge

The airline faced fragmented systems and disjointed workflows in its customer service centers. Agents struggled to provide consistent, timely assistance due to the lack of an integrated solution, leading to slower issue resolution and reduced customer satisfaction. A scalable, multi-channel support platform was required to address these inefficiencies.

Solution

1. Strategy & Vision

The transformation journey began with a two-month discovery phase focused on:

  • Analyzing the current state of operations.
  • Identifying gaps in service delivery.
  • Defining a future state vision for seamless customer and agent experiences.

2. Design & Pilot

A unified service console was developed to empower service representatives with:

  • A consolidated view of crucial customer, loyalty, and flight data.
  • An intuitive interface designed to enhance agent productivity.

3. Launch & Refine

Within four months, the airline introduced a Mobile Live Chat feature, adding a new support channel for its Southwest Rapid Rewards Members. This enabled real-time customer assistance while enhancing accessibility.

4. Optimize & Scale

Plans were set in motion to expand the solution’s capabilities by:

  • Rolling out the service console to 4,000 phone agents across 11 customer service centers.
  • Expanding access to two additional departments in future releases, further scaling the platform.

Results

The implementation of the Salesforce Customer360 Service Console brought substantial improvements:

  • 180,000 chat interactions recorded since the platform’s go-live.
  • 100% increase in the ability to support in-flight customers, elevating service quality.
  • Support extended to five channels, including voice, email, web chat, social media, and mobile live chat.

Impact Metrics:

  • Customer Experience: 5/5
  • Employee Engagement: 5/5
  • Productivity: 5/5
  • Growth: 3/5

Conclusion

This case study highlights how the Salesforce Customer360 Service Console transformed customer service operations for a major airline. By unifying data, introducing new support channels, and optimizing workflows, the airline significantly enhanced its ability to provide exceptional service. This initiative stands as a testament to the value of digital innovation in driving superior customer experiences in the aviation sector.

title.rendered: Enhancing B2B Engagement with a Centralized Sales Portal

content.rendered:
Introduction

A global airline leader aimed to transform its B2B engagement by modernizing its outdated centralized sales platform. The goal was to simplify travel management for corporate clients and travel agencies, streamline administrative processes, and enable advanced servicing capabilities. Collaborating with a global consulting firm, the airline implemented a centralized Salesforce-powered platform, creating a seamless experience for its B2B customers.

Challenge

The airline’s legacy systems lacked integration and scalability, causing inefficiencies for travel managers and agency partners. Administrative sales tasks consumed excessive time, and limited functionalities hindered effective customer servicing. A centralized sales solution was needed to improve usability, reduce manual tasks, and unlock new revenue opportunities.

Solution

1. Strategy & Vision

The project began with a one-month discovery phase to:

  • Validate system requirements and align stakeholders on key objectives.
  • Develop a digital proof of concept and establish the technical environment for the centralized sales platform.

2. Design & Pilot

The consulting team collaborated with business SMEs to design a portal prototype for a smaller user group. Key features included:

  • Security controls for user data and portal access.
  • CRM foundation integration to provide a unified view of customer data.
  • Initial reporting capabilities to deliver actionable insights.

3. Launch & Refine

The portal was expanded to include:

  • Amenity banking: Enabling easy management of additional services.
  • Servicing knowledge base: Providing quick access to critical information for customer support.
  • Extended reporting capabilities: Allowing detailed analysis of sales and customer engagement.

4. Optimize & Scale

The final phase focused on further enhancement and scalability by introducing:

  • Contract lifecycle management tools for streamlined deal execution.
  • Advanced customer servicing capabilities to meet diverse client needs efficiently.

Results

The implementation of the centralized sales portal, known as Jetstream, delivered substantial improvements:

  • 150% increase in portal traffic compared to the previous system.
  • 18% reduction in weekly administrative sales activities, cutting hours down to minutes.
  • Over $22 million in transactions processed through the Jetstream platform.

Impact Metrics:

  • Customer Experience: 5/5
  • Employee Engagement: 3/5
  • Productivity: 5/5
  • Growth: 4/5

Conclusion

This case study demonstrates the transformative power of a centralized Salesforce solution in the airline industry. By modernizing its centralized sales platform, the airline enhanced its B2B customer experience, improved operational efficiency, and unlocked new revenue streams. The Jetstream platform stands as a testament to the value of digital innovation in optimizing corporate travel management and customer engagement.

title.rendered: Transforming the Timeshare Industry with a Digitized Tour Management Platform

content.rendered:
Introduction

A leading company in the timeshare industry revolutionized its operations by digitizing its tour management platform. The goal was to eliminate outdated manual processes, enhance customer experiences, and empower leadership with a 360-degree view of guest and owner data. Collaborating with a global consulting firm, the company successfully implemented a Salesforce-powered solution that streamlined operations, reduced costs, and drove productivity.

Challenge

Operating in a highly competitive industry, the company faced challenges stemming from legacy systems inherited through multiple acquisitions. These systems were inefficient, resulting in lengthy booking processes, increased marketing spend, and a lack of real-time data access. The need for a unified, paperless platform became critical to maintaining its market leadership.

Solution

  1. Strategy & Vision
    The transformation began with a thorough assessment of the company’s business processes and legacy systems. This included:
  • Reviewing the architecture of inherited systems to identify inefficiencies.
  • Establishing a framework for digitization that prioritized scalability and ease of use.
  1. Design & Pilot
    A pilot program introduced cutting-edge functionality tailored to the company’s needs, including:
  • Real-time slot availability: Allowing for instant updates on tour schedules.
  • Instant notifications for sales representatives: Ensuring quick responses to customer needs.
  • Control of the tour life cycle: Automating processes from booking to feedback collection.
  1. Launch & Refine
    The integrated tour management system was launched, offering:
  • Paperless processes: Eliminating the need for manual documentation.
  • Dynamic dashboards: Providing real-time insights for better decision-making.
  • Real-time availability updates: Improving scheduling efficiency for guests and employees.
  1. Optimize & Scale
    Following the launch, the company conducted ongoing feedback analysis to:
  • Fine-tune processes and ensure seamless integration across multiple brands.
  • Maintain system efficiency and adapt to evolving business requirements.

Results

The digitized tour management platform delivered impressive results:

  • 85,000 leads generated within six months of going live.
  • 5-minute reduction in the time required to book a tour.
  • 18,000 tours booked in a single month following the platform’s launch.

Impact Metrics:

  • Customer Experience: 5/5
  • Employee Engagement: 5/5
  • Productivity: 4/5
  • Growth: 5/5

Conclusion

This case study demonstrates how digitizing a core business process can transform an entire industry. By leveraging Salesforce’s capabilities, the company not only enhanced its operational efficiency but also redefined the customer experience in the timeshare industry. This digital transformation serves as a blueprint for organizations looking to innovate and scale seamlessly.

title.rendered: Redefining Front Office Operations to Realize Synergies for a Global Food Conglomerate

content.rendered:
Introduction

A Global Food Conglomerate sought to seamlessly integrate its commercial functions after acquiring another major brand. The challenge was to redefine its operating model for sales, marketing, and innovation teams while leveraging Salesforce multi-cloud solutions to achieve operational synergies and enhance customer engagement. This transformation would enable the company to deliver a flawless close and unlock significant value.

Challenge

The integration of two large organizations presented several complexities, including:

  • Merging disparate systems and processes for sales, marketing, and consumer care.
  • Standardizing trade spend practices and renegotiating broker contracts.
  • Aligning strategic goals to achieve a seamless front office transformation at “deal speed.”

Solution

  1. Strategy & Vision
    The project began by translating the company’s strategic goals into actionable integration design principles. Key steps included:
  • Conducting cost and capability benchmarking to identify opportunities for improvement.
  • Defining a roadmap to ensure that the front office transformation would align with the acquisition timeline.
  1. Design & Pilot
    To prepare for integration, the team developed a comprehensive plan for “Day 1” readiness, including:

Challenge

  • Automated out-of-stock reviews to improve inventory management.
  1. Optimize & Scale
    The Salesforce platform was architected for standardization, minimizing the need for extensive customizations while allowing for localized configurations. This approach enabled:

Results

The integrated platform delivered remarkable outcomes:

  • 20% increase in productivity, enabling employees to focus on value-adding activities.
  • 100% adoption of the solution within 45 days of rollout.
  • Deployment across 16 countries, ensuring a consistent and scalable retail execution model.

Impact Metrics:

  • Customer Experience: 5/5
  • Employee Engagement: 5/5
  • Productivity: 5/5
  • Growth: 4/5

Conclusion

This transformation demonstrates how an integrated Salesforce solution can enhance retail execution, optimize productivity, and drive sales growth. By focusing on user experience, standardization, and regional adaptability, the company successfully achieved consistent results across Latin America. This LATAM Productivity Case Study serves as a model for leveraging technology to overcome operational inefficiencies and achieve scalable growth.

title.rendered: Enabling a Global Food and Beverage Leader`s New Go-To-Market Strategy

content.rendered:
Introduction

A global leader in the food and beverage industry needed to redefine its go-to-market (GTM) strategy. The main goals were to increase market share, improve sales processes, and achieve distribution savings. By using Salesforce, the company aimed to optimize its Direct Store Delivery (DSD) system. This change would drive productivity across its sales teams and enhance front office operations. To achieve these objectives, a leading global consulting firm partnered with the company to design and implement a comprehensive GTM strategy that would impact its entire sales function.

Challenge

The company’s existing sales and distribution system lacked efficiency and scalability. Fragmented processes, slow in-store execution, and inadequate data analytics hindered operations and affected competitiveness. As a result, the company needed a solution that could optimize sales productivity, streamline retail execution, and provide real-time insights into operations.

Solution

  1. Strategy & Vision
    The consulting firm began with a 3-week blueprint phase. During this phase, they defined the strategic fit for DSD technology transformation. They carefully mapped out key program decisions—including strategy, processes, and IT framework—to ensure alignment with the company’s broader business goals.
  2. Design & Pilot
    Next, the consulting firm collaborated closely with the client. They used Salesforce’s global templates and agile methodologies to launch a pilot program in key regions such as Mexico, Brazil, and CASA. The team customized the solution for each region to meet local market needs. This pilot focused on streamlining retail execution and improving in-store efficiency through the Salesforce-powered system.
  3. Launch & Refine
    The transformation continued with developing a mobile front end for MC1. Within 6 months, the minimum viable product (MVP) was released, which significantly decreased average visit time. Additionally, Salesforce CRM and Business Analytics Platform (BAP) were integrated to support the transformation. This integration allowed sales representatives to access real-time data and make informed decisions on the go.
  4. Optimize & Scale
    The solution was then scaled across the region, extending its reach to over 15 countries in LATAM. With a focus on developing advanced capabilities in agile program increments, the company began to see savings from more efficient processes and optimized resources.

Results

The Salesforce-powered solution delivered significant improvements across the organization:

  • 4% increase in incremental revenue through optimized credit management.
  • 120 minutes saved daily for sales representatives, allowing them to focus on more valuable activities.
  • Over 7.8 million customer visits recorded on the platform to date, demonstrating wide adoption and success.

Impact Metrics:

  • Customer Experience: 5/5
  • Employee Engagement: 5/5
  • Productivity: 5/5
  • Growth: 4/5

Conclusion

This case study highlights how leveraging Salesforce’s powerful suite of tools can transform sales operations and drive business growth. By implementing a comprehensive cloud-based solution across key regions, the company achieved impressive productivity gains while aligning its sales processes with its new go-to-market strategy. With a clear focus on agile development and localization, the company rapidly scaled and optimized its front office. As a result, it made significant strides toward achieving its global business objectives.

title.rendered: Digital Transformation of a Leading Global Professional Services Firm’s Front Office

content.rendered:
Introduction

A prominent global professional services firm embarked on a bold journey of digital transformation to stay competitive in a rapidly evolving market. As part of its vision to become a digitally enabled organization, the firm aimed to unify its global network, streamline business processes, and equip employees with the tools necessary to thrive in an increasingly disruptive business environment.

Challenge

The firm faced several challenges that necessitated this transformation. With a global workforce and an extensive market reach across multiple countries, the existing systems and processes were not scalable or agile enough to keep up with the demands of a digital-first world. The need for an integrated, cloud-based platform to streamline operations and improve employee productivity and engagement became critical.

Solution

1. Strategy & Vision

To kickstart the transformation, the firm developed a comprehensive business case and a multi-year digital roadmap. Leadership alignment was crucial to ensure that the entire organization embraced the transformation vision. This roadmap focused on establishing a foundation of cloud technologies and leading business processes that would serve as the backbone for the front office transformation.

2. Design & Pilot

The firm fostered a culture of continuous improvement and real-time feedback, supported by digital coaching and performance management tools. A new talent brand, The Professional, was launched, which emphasized a commitment to digital learning and growth. The pilot phase included the introduction of custom learning tools such as:

  • Salesforce Digital Lab
  • Digital Fitness Assessment app
  • Learning Bursts
  • Digital Quests
  • PowerUp Trivia Challenges

These tools helped employees engage with the digital transformation and adopt new processes more efficiently.

3. Launch & Refine

The transformation was focused on leadership-driven change, incorporating leadership tools that encouraged engagement at every level of the organization. Custom learning modules, such as the Digital Academy and the Digital Accelerator Program, provided targeted training on priority technologies for specialists across various regions.

4. Optimize & Scale

As the initiative progressed, the focus shifted to optimizing and scaling the new digital tools. Firmwide upskilling sessions like the Digital Academy were rolled out globally, helping employees continuously adapt to emerging technologies and processes.

Results

The transformation achieved significant results across the global network:

  • 100% adoption across the global network of employees.
  • Successful implementation in 158 countries, impacting a workforce of over 236,000 employees.
  • The new tools and systems fostered significant improvements in employee engagement, productivity, and overall business growth.

Impact Metrics:

  • Customer Experience: 3/5
  • Employee Engagement: 5/5
  • Productivity: 5/5
  • Growth: 5/5

Conclusion

This large-scale front office transformation illustrates how a global organization can leverage cloud-based technologies and innovative learning tools to create a unified, digitally enabled workforce. By focusing on leadership-driven change and employee upskilling, the firm has set the stage for continued success in a competitive, digital-first business landscape.
